comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results. Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.

With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

issues.descricao: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

comentarios.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.

Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

issues.descricao: The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

comentarios.texto: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

issues.descricao: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc says only LOGS is supported, although the hooks are also used with SPANS.

comentarios.texto: The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

issues.descricao: Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.
dedupedYAxes is now just [yAxis], so its name misdescribes the code.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.

sugestoes.texto: The cache-hit branch of `getForLogin` returns raw `IdentityProviderModel` objects from `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, so `isEnabled()` no longer reflects the linked organization's state and an org-linked IDP whose organization is disabled is reported as enabled again once the cache is warm. Wrap the resolved model on the cache-hit path with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(idp)` to match the cache-miss branches at lines 218 and 249.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

sugestoes.texto: Because `clean()` still executes all eight maintenance jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) under a shared 9-minute timeout, every one of them now runs up to ten times more often, multiplying DB and filesystem load on every Grafana instance — and the annotation job in this same PR adds a SELECT plus DELETE round-trip per batch that deliberately tolerates deleting nothing on a given cycle. Revert the ticker to the original 10-minute interval, or split the annotation cleanup onto its own schedule/config instead of speeding up the whole job set.

issues.descricao: Leftover debug logs in the annotation cleanup emit Error-level entries with the full ID list on every batch, flooding error logs during normal operation.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls r.log.Error on every cleanup batch (also duplicated at lines 554-557 and 576-579) dumping full ids slice, cond, and nil err at Error level. WHY: Fires Error-level log per batch and serializes up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs (32767 in new test), spamming error logs/monitoring on every normal cleanup run. HOW: Downgrade to Debug or remove; do not log full ids at Error.

WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` (and the identical Error-level logs for 'by count' and 'Tags to clean', lines 554/557/576/579) run on every batch in production. WHY: These log the full ID slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 elements) at Error severity on every cleanup iteration, flooding logs with false error noise and large payloads for a normal successful operation, and can trigger error-based alerting. HOW: Remove these log lines, or downgrade to Debug and drop the full `ids` slice (log only the count).

Avoid using Error-level logging on the normal cleanup path. The new r.log.Error calls emit count, ids, cond, and err at lines 534/537, 554/557, and 576/579 during non-error execution, creating log noise; consider downgrading or removing these logs on the normal path.

issues.descricao: The comment states SQLite's parameter limit is 999, which is only true for SQLite versions before 3.32.0.

comentarios.texto: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

issues.descricao: On MySQL and Postgres, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID without limit, so a cleanup batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.

comentarios.texto: The bind-parameter workaround only handles SQLite's limit; the placeholder branch is used for every other engine with len(ids) placeholders and no bound. The previous implementation had no bind parameters, so this path is new. Postgres (extended protocol) and MySQL both cap bind parameters at 65535, so a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize larger than that makes this DELETE fail at Exec with a parameter-limit error instead of cleaning anything. Clamp the number of ids per DELETE (e.g. chunk into <=1000/<=65535 id sub-batches) for all dialects, not just SQLite.

On Postgres and MySQL, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535) makes every cleanup batch fail, and the cleanup job then never finishes. Split the IDs into chunks below the limit, or inline the integer IDs as the SQLite branch does.

issues.descricao: The SQLite inline ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: SQLite large-batch IN-list built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. WHY: Quadratic string copying on large batches (e.g. 32767 IDs in added test) during cleanup, a background job path. HOW: Build with strings.Builder or strings.Join.

The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

issues.descricao: The cleanup service ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often and increasing database load.
issues.textoGolden: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification. WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.descricao: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.

sugestoes.texto: The caching sentinel logic in the service is now completely untested, so a regression that rebuilds conditions on every call or returns stale conditions can ship without any test failing. Re-add the caching tests using the new `Prisma.sql` expectations (first call builds the condition, second call returns an equal value), mirroring the routing service suite.

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

sugestoes.texto: `ensure_loaded!` is only defined on the `FallbackLocaleList` instance that config/initializers/i18n.rb assigns to `I18n.fallbacks`, so any environment where that initializer has not populated `I18n.fallbacks` with a `FallbackLocaleList` (the initializer file failing to load before `set_locale` runs, a reload in dev/test/console, or Rails reassigning `I18n.fallbacks`) raises `NoMethodError` on every request. Guard the call with `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! if I18n.fallbacks.respond_to?(:ensure_loaded!)`, or move the preload into the backend itself so it does not depend on a specific `I18n.fallbacks` type.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

issues.descricao: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, so the feature guard in the check subcommand is untested.

comentarios.texto: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the `metadata` subcommand and never the `check` subcommand. Removing the feature guard from UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() would therefore not fail any test. It also doesn't assert the exit code (FEATURE_DISABLED=4). Add a case for `check` and assert the exit code on both.

WHAT: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand disabled path and never the check subcommand. WHY: the feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run can be removed or broken without failing any test since no assertion covers its disabled message/exit code. HOW: also launch/assert the check command without --features (e.g. parameterize over metadata and check subcommands or add a second Launch).

testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand, leaving the identical ROLLING_UPDATES gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck unverified. If the Check gate were removed, the suite still passes. Parameterize/add a second @Launch for {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME} (with required --file or not) asserting the disabled message and FEATURE_DISABLED exit code.

issues.descricao: The disabled-feature test checks only the error message, not that the command exits with FEATURE_DISABLED (4).

comentarios.texto: The new disabled-feature test only verifies the error text, not the failure exit status. If the metadata command still prints this diagnostic but exits with 0 (or another incorrect code) instead of FEATURE_DISABLED (4), this test would still pass. Assert that cliResult.exitCode() equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED so the test actually protects the new disabled-feature failure contract.

issues.descricao: testMissingOptionOnSave only asserts a message is absent, so it would still pass if --features=rolling-updates were not honoured and the command failed with the feature-disabled error.
The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets holds a global exclusive mutex through the whole manifest load, so in Dev mode, where the cache is bypassed, every request serializes behind it.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.

comentarios.texto: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

comentarios.texto: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which never existed in IE/Edge; the legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so the declaration is dead.
issues.textoGolden: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a valid IE10/11 property (only -ms-flex-align exists). WHY: dead declaration shows wrong contract and leaves IE alignment dependent solely on -ms-flex-align, which also breaks for flex-start/flex-end values. HOW: remove the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align.

issues.descricao: Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.
issues.textoGolden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

The singular branch (line 146) returns a `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` value such as "A missed check-in was detected", yet the docstring advertises "A failed check-in was detected"; the multi-check-in branch joins `"%(count)d %(status)s"` fragments with `get_text_list(..., last_word=_("and"))` and appends " check-ins detected", yielding "2 missed and 1 error check-ins detected", not the docstring's "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". Update the examples (or the format string) so the documented contract matches the code.

issues.descricao: get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy with the human-readable schedule_type but returns the original monitor.config, so the conversion is lost and the context shows the raw value.
issues.textoGolden: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config to `config` and converts schedule_type display, but returns the original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of `config`. WHY: the display conversion never takes effect so the occurrence context carries the raw schedule_type value, producing wrong output vs the function's evident intent. HOW: return `"config": config` instead of `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

Dead computation: `config` is copied and `config['schedule_type']` transformed to display value, but return uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (original) instead of `config`. Change to `"config": config` so transformation is used.

WHAT: In get_monitor_environment_context the code copies config and replaces config['schedule_type'] with the human-readable get_schedule_type_display(), but the returned context dict uses the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified local `config`, so the mutation is dead. WHY: The occurrence's monitor context always reports the raw schedule_type value rather than the display string the code intended to substitute, producing incorrect evidence data in the emitted occurrence. HOW: return the local variable, i.e. use "config": config in the returned dict.

issues.descricao: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the light-theme color changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70% because the dark-light-choose arguments were inverted, making the link much paler in light themes.
issues.textoGolden: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

comentarios.texto: The light-theme argument was changed from the original lightness. WHAT: the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new value uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the first (light-theme) argument is now 70%, not 30%. WHY: this silently darkens the light-theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` (post-author link) from a 30% to a 70% tint, a light-theme regression outside the PR's dark-theme-only intent; the values also are inverted relative to the (X, 100−X) convention used everywhere else (should be 30/70). HOW: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

The original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). After conversion the light-mode argument became $primary:70% and dark-mode $secondary:30% — both inverted away from the original 30%. Should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). As written the light-mode color is dramatically lighter than intended.

issues.descricao: In dark themes the notification badge background becomes a lightened $secondary while its text stays $secondary, giving dark text on a dark background with poor contrast.

comentarios.texto: The dark-theme notification badge background now uses a lightened $secondary while its text still uses the unmodified $secondary. This puts dark text on a dark background for plain badges such as category unread counts in site-map.hbs:73; with $secondary black, the foreground is #000 and the background is approximately #4d4d4d (about 2.5:1 contrast), making the small count text difficult to read. Set the default badge foreground, including its &[href] rule, to a contrasting dark-theme color such as $primary when selecting this dark background.
